# Tools and charts

Chart-family counts reflect source image labels, not an exact count of every conceptual reference or a measure of forecasting value. Representative chart notes reflect actual visual inspection; all chart images remain with the original publishers.

| Family | Reports | Use | Observed labels |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business cycle | 149 | Growth rates and breadth: distinguish a slowdown from contraction. | GDPNow, Economic Heatmap, ISM PMI, Jobless Claims, GDP Now |
| Domestic liquidity | 111 | Separate Fed assets, Treasury cash, money-fund balances and bank funding. | Domestic Liquidity, Fed Balance Sheet, TGA, Treasury General Account, Bank Cash Levels |
| Valuation and cash flow | 175 | Compare price with earnings, cash generation and historical multiples. | EPD FASTGraph, ITUB FASTGraph, ADBE FASTGraph, CI FASTGraph, USB FASTGraph |
| Global money and currencies | 109 | Connect dollar funding, local liquidity, currencies and international assets. | Dollar Index, DXY, Global M2, Bitcoin vs Global M2, USDJPY |
| Bitcoin ownership and valuation | 87 | Use ownership and cost-basis proxies alongside liquidity and adoption. | Bitcoin MVRV, HODL Wave, Bitcoin HODL Wave, RHODL Ratio, MVRV Z-Score |
| Energy and commodity supply | 45 | Track inventories, production, capacity and long investment cycles. | WTI Crude, US Oil Production, Strategic Petroleum Reserve, Uranium Price, Uranium Chart |
| Gold and real yields | 19 | Distinguish inflation compensation, real interest rates and monetary hedges. | Gold vs Real Rates, Treasury vs TIPS, Gold vs Real Rates Longterm, Real Rates, TIPS Real Yield |

## Representative chart interpretations

### Domestic Liquidity

Report 181 | 2026-02-01

Inspected FRED net-liquidity chart: Fed assets minus TGA minus reverse repos, with unit scaling. Treat as an accounting proxy, not money available to buy stocks or proof of price causation. Components differ in frequency and institutional function.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2026-2-1-domestic-liquidity.png) | [Article review](articles/181.md)

### Bitcoin MVRV

Report 190 | 2026-06-07

Inspected dual-axis MVRV Z-score: market/realized cap on log USD axis, Z-score on right. Valuation zones are historical heuristics, not guaranteed floors, ceilings or a cash-flow valuation.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2026-6-7-bitcoin-mvrv.png) | [Article review](articles/190.md)

### Economic Heatmap

Report 136 | 2024-05-12

Inspected rolling heatmap: indicators use five-year relative color ranges, newest observations at top; CPI uses a distinct blue/white/red palette. Some series are nominal and need inflation adjustment. A red cell need not mean absolute contraction.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2024-5-12-economic-heatmap.png) | [Article review](articles/136.md)

### Gold vs Real Rates

Report 076 | 2022-01-23

Inspected gold/real-rate dual-axis plot. Opposite visual movement can be useful context but depends on period, axis scaling and regime. Gold is not a mechanical function of a single real-rate series.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2022-1-23-gold-real-rates.png) | [Article review](articles/076.md)

### EPD FASTGraph

Report 198 | 2026-09-27

Inspected EPD FASTgraphs: operating EPS, historical valuation multiple, selected fair-value multiple, prices and dividends. Future EPS/dividend rows marked E and dotted paths are estimates, not realized results. A normal historical multiple is not an objective intrinsic value.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2026-9-27-epd-fastgraph.png) | [Article review](articles/198.md)

### Global M2

Report 192 | 2026-07-05

Inspected global M2: USD-denominated level on left and annual percentage growth on right. Currency translation and changing growth rates matter separately from the level. A rising stock of money does not establish a near-term asset-price prediction.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2026-7-5-m2.png) | [Article review](articles/192.md)

### China Credit Impulse

Report 182 | 2026-02-15

Inspected China credit impulse/housing plot. Credit impulse is a flow acceleration signal, not the debt stock. Different axes and a small number of historical cycles limit causal inference and lag selection.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2026-2-15-china-credit-impulse.png) | [Article review](articles/182.md)

### MVRV versus two-year returns

Report 166 | 2025-07-06

Inspected full and 200%-capped scatterplots covering July 2014-July 2023 starting dates. Daily two-year forward returns overlap heavily, so thousands of dots are not thousands of independent tests. A few Bitcoin cycles dominate the sample. The capped panel reveals losses more clearly but cannot establish a valuation floor or correct for changing market maturity; even moderate MVRV values have negative two-year outcomes.

[Original chart](https://www.lynalden.com/wp-content/uploads/premium-2025-7-6-mvrv-vs-2year-returns.png) | [Article review](articles/166.md)

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning | What to watch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TGA | Treasury General Account: the U.S. government’s account at the Federal Reserve. | A rising balance drains bank reserves if other balance-sheet items are unchanged. Offsetting flows matter. |
| Bank reserves | Balances eligible banks hold at the central bank for settlement and liquidity. | They are distinct from household deposits and are not mechanically lent out to create a fixed amount of credit. |
| Overnight RRP | A Fed facility in which eligible counterparties temporarily place cash against securities. | A falling balance can offset reserve drains elsewhere. Money funds and banks hold different claims. |
| QT and Fed purchases | QT lets securities holdings run down. Purchases add securities and matching liabilities. | Reserve-management purchases and monetary easing can differ in purpose and maturity; size alone does not identify the policy stance. |
| Fiscal dominance | A setting in which government financing constraints strongly influence monetary policy. | It is a hypothesis about constraints and incentives, not proof that rates cannot rise or that every rate hike stimulates growth. |
| Real yields | Returns after inflation; TIPS yields provide a market-based real-yield measure. | Expected and realized inflation differ. TIPS prices also reflect liquidity and risk premia. |
| Yield curve | Interest rates across maturities, often summarized by a long-minus-short spread. | Inversion is a warning signal with variable lead times, not a uniquely timed recession forecast. |
| Credit spread | The yield difference between risky debt and a comparison instrument. | Match maturity and other features. The spread reflects liquidity and risk compensation as well as default expectations. |
| Credit impulse | A measure of acceleration or deceleration in new credit, usually scaled to economic output. | A slowing impulse can coexist with a growing debt stock. Definitions and currency translation vary. |
| Global M2 | An aggregation of broad-money measures across countries, often translated into dollars. | Country coverage, definitions and exchange rates affect the result. It is not a single globally spendable pool. |
| MVRV | Bitcoin market value divided by realized value, which revalues coins when they last moved. | Coin movement is not always a purchase. Historical valuation bands are not guaranteed price floors. |
| CAPE | Price relative to a long average of inflation-adjusted earnings, commonly ten years. | Useful for valuation context; accounting, sector mix and interest rates complicate comparisons and short-term timing. |
| FAST Graphs | Charts combining share price, company fundamentals, valuation multiples and estimates. | The historical multiple is a reference, and future earnings points are forecasts. Neither is guaranteed fair value. |
| SLR | Supplementary leverage ratio: a capital backstop based on total leverage exposure. | It differs from risk-weighted capital ratios. Cash reserves, bank capital and Treasury risk weights are different concepts. |
| Capital cycle | Investment changes future supply, often with a long delay in physical industries. | Low investment can support future returns, but only if demand, costs, access and the selected investment vehicle cooperate. |
